card.name: Govend
card.tagline: Kurdish communal hand-holding circle dance of celebration and identity
card.profile: Govend (also gowend, halparke, helperke, dilan) is the general Kurdish term for the communal hand-holding circle/line dance, the joyful heart of Kurdish weddings, Newroz and festivals (Kurdish dance, Wikipedia). Dancers link hands, shoulders or interlocked pinky fingers and follow a leader (sergovend/sercopi) who often waves a handkerchief, moving from slow stately steps to fast, exhilarating sequences, typically accompanied by zurna and davul/daf (The Kurdish Project; Kurdish dance, Wikipedia). It is danced across Iraqi Kurdistan and in Turkey, Syria and Iran, and is notably mixed-gender, distinguishing it from neighboring traditions; it is closely related to halay and dabke (Kurdish dance, Wikipedia).
card.insight: In Sorani the dance is called copi (chopee), led by a sercopi - etymologically linking govend to the wider Iraqi chobi/chopi line-dance family (The Kurdish Project).

observation.dancers: A group of male dancers in matching traditional attire, plus one small child and a soloist in front
observation.formation_and_space: A straight line of dancers holding arms/shoulders side by side, performing synchronized steps and dropping low together
observation.posture: Upright torso, slight knee bends, upright stance shifting weight collectively
observation.footwork: Stepping sideways and stamping or tapping on beats in unison
observation.arms_and_hands: Linked at shoulders or arms interlaced in a line; soloist holds a small red flag/prop
observation.hips_and_torso: Minimal hip movement, torso remains upright and bends forward together when lowering
observation.partnering: Group contact in a line holding shoulders/arms
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Standing and periodic synchronized deep squats/kneeling to the floor in unison
observation.costume_and_props: Matching grey traditional tunic and baggy trousers (shalwar kameez), headwear, white shoes; red flag held by soloist and child
